AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVES
AbstractText.content: To review the etiology, evaluation, and treatment of hirsutism.

AbstractText.Label: EVALUATION
AbstractText.content: A thorough history and physical examination plus selected laboratory evaluations will confirm the diagnosis and direct treatment.

AbstractText.Label: TREATMENT
AbstractText.content: Pharmacologic interventions can suppress ovarian or adrenal androgen production and block androgen receptors in the hair follicle. Hair removal methods and lifestyle modifications may improve or hasten the therapeutic response.

AbstractText.Label: OUTCOMES
AbstractText.content: At least 6 to 9 months of therapy are required to produce improvement in hirsutism.

AbstractText.Label: EVIDENCE
AbstractText.content: The quality of evidence reported in this guideline has been determined using the criteria described by the Canadian Task Force on the Periodic Health Examination.

AbstractText.Label: RECOMMENDATIONS
AbstractText.content: Hirsutism can be slowly but dramatically improved with a 3-pronged approach to treatment: mechanical hair removal, suppression of androgen production, and androgen receptor blockade. Lifestyle changes, including weight loss and exercise, will lower serum androgen levels and improve self-esteem in patients with polycystic ovary syndrome. The patient should be educated regarding the associated health problems or long-term medical consequences of hyperandrogenism, particularly in the context of polycystic ovary syndrome, including obesity, irregular menses, anovulation, infertility, pregnancy-induced hypertension, diabetes, hyperlipidemia, hypertension, and heart disease.
